paper.title: AutoVQA-G: Self-Improving Agentic Framework for Automated Visual Question Answering and Grounding Annotation
paper.central_claim: Memory-augmented, critique-directed generation-rubric optimization produces more consistent and accurately grounded VQA-G annotations than single-pass leading VLMs, efficiently elevating a small generator.
paper.scope_reason: Eqs10–11 explicitly retain and edit generation rubrics plus optimizer history for the next generation round; this is a non-weight harness-state update, not only answer rewriting. Its demonstrated horizon is nevertheless the same-image episode. No cross-image retention or later-task benefit is inferred; evidence_level remains task. The reusable prompt optimizer also fits the B-component definition.

signatures.object: Caption/VQA/VG generation-rubric texts and historical optimizer memory
signatures.information: Current image, generated question/answer/mention/box, two CoT vision critiques, previous rubric/draft/critique history
signatures.operation: Generate modular annotation; score image-text and image-box consistency; if below threshold diagnose failure, select one module, and apply a localized rubric edit; retain revised rubric and history for next round
signatures.output: Revised module rubric and a new VQA-G draft
signatures.conditions: Frozen MiniCPM-o2.6 generator, GroundingDINO localizer, Qwen2.5-VL72B verifier and DeepSeekV3 optimizer
signatures.feedback: Two model-generated stepwise consistency scores plus verbal critiques; 0.7 VQA/0.3 VG aggregate
signatures.selection_rule: Accept annotation if score>=0.9; maximum five iterations then choose best result; no independent rubric-utility gate or rollback described
signatures.persistence: R(t+1) and H(t) persist to subsequent rounds within one image; cross-image initialization/retention unspecified
signatures.later_use: Regenerate annotation with amended rubrics for same input image
signatures.claimed_effect: Fewer hallucinations, higher consistency and grounding quality
signatures.failure_boundary: Proxy certification, changed query ambiguity, extra large models and retries; no later-task retained/improver evidence

signatures.selection_rule: Weighted score threshold or best of five

gap.author_gap: Single-pass VQA-G synthesis hallucinates and heuristic verification is brittle.
gap.checked_gap: A concrete annotation-fidelity bottleneck and a relevant loop are described. The nearest prompt-optimization frameworks are cited as inspiration, but their originals are unavailable and a new general improver is not established.

Existing feedback-driven prompt rewrite skeleton; original sources not independently checked

gap.stakes: Annotation cost and evidential grounding for VLM datasets.
gap.method_response: Explicit verifier/optimizer roles replace heuristic acceptance and static single-pass rubrics.
gap.remaining_gap: No demonstrated cross-image reusable improvement, independently certified attribution accuracy, or matched-budget alternative prompt optimizer.

claims.text: AutoVQA-G outperforms leading VLMs in annotation quality and consistency.
claims.setting: Visual7W and VizWiz; 10,000 source images, allocation unclear; human grounding reannotation 500 per method/dataset, 6,000 total
claims.baseline_control: GPT4o ZS with same GroundingDINO plus native GPT4o/Gemini ZS/CoT baselines
claims.selection_vs_test: Per-image drafts selected by learned consistency; validation tuned threshold/weights/round cap; split identities unspecified
claims.result_denominator: Visual7W full mIoU .634/Acc .720/VQAG .747 vs tool baseline .455/.510/.669; VizWiz .649/.680/.737 vs .472/.525/.667
counterevidence: Visual7W TIFA .819 below human .865 and all model baselines; VQAScore .896 below tool baseline .923. VizWiz VQAScore .874 below .907. No CIs. Non-success inclusion unclear.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Better reported grounding and aggregate score for selected generated questions, not uniform superiority on VQA fidelity, identical questions, or dataset coverage.

claims.text: History-aware targeted prompt optimization improves annotation quality.
claims.baseline_control: No loop, score-only, no routing, no memory
claims.selection_vs_test: Evaluation is the same generation/selection episode; no frozen revised-rubric later-image test
claims.result_denominator: Full VQAScore/mIoU .896/.634; no loop .863/.380; score-only .879/.495; no routing .875/.561; no memory .885/.582; ablation sample denominator not restated
counterevidence: No fixed-budget extra-sampling control or full factorial; no attribution accuracy or repeat variance
claims.allowed_conclusion: Ablations support contributions to task-level episode output; no causal retained benefit on later tasks or improved improver mechanism.

claims.text: Small-generator framework is resource-efficient and scalable.
claims.setting: Four local RTX4090 plus remote72B verifier and DeepSeekV3 optimizer, maxfive rounds
claims.baseline_control: Single-pass larger-model methods, no matched total resources
claims.result_denominator: Success91.8/89.2%; 1.62/2.15 rounds and2.1K/3.1K tokens per success
counterevidence: Large auxiliary models, unknown failed-attempt costs, no end-to-end latency/dollar baseline
claims.allowed_conclusion: Partial operating-cost description only, not established relative cost effectiveness or downstream training benefit.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Authors report higher selected-annotation grounding scores on two datasets, with local rubric/history ablations supporting within-image refinement. Retained prompt state exists between rounds, but no measured later-image reuse, no retained-level or improver-level benefit, and no independent reproduction.

Cross-image prompt/history lifecycle, validation split, non-success inclusion and full auxiliary-model costs unspecified.

G.reason: Real annotation-fidelity bottleneck, but nearest optimizer lineage and distinctive gap remain only partly established.

M.reason: Critique-to-selected-rubric edit is reconstructable and relevant; diagnosis accuracy and distinction from ordinary rewrite/retry remain weakly tested.

X.reason: Explicit modular interfaces, state, update equation, scoring, threshold and stop rule; cross-image lifecycle and exact linked templates not provided.

E.measurement.reason: Human grounding reannotation and multiple VQA metrics are relevant; uncalibrated judge, variable easier queries and unclear non-success denominator constrain interpretation.

E.causality.reason: Four ablations and shared-tool comparison relevant, but unmatched large auxiliary models, retries and no equal-budget static-rubric control.

E.holdout.reason: Two datasets, but rubric is optimized and selected on the current image; validation split unspecified and no retained-rubric independent later-image test. This is task evidence, not retained.

E.statistics.reason: Sample sizes and negative VQA-metric findings reported; main comparisons and ablations lack seeds, uncertainty or significance. A2 step1.

E.cost.reason: Success-only token/iteration averages plus overhead concession; no full failed-attempt, large-verifier/optimizer, latency or monetary accounting.

reason: Full available fixed-version paper read. Explicit rubric/history updates meet non-weight next-round persistence; final annotation gains are scoped task evidence, not later-task retained improvement.
